question:
A factory produces three types of products: A, B, and C. Each unit of product A requires 1 hour of technical preparation, 10 hours of direct labor, and 3 kilograms of material. Each unit of product B requires 2 hours of technical preparation, 4 hours of labor, and 2 kilograms of material. Each unit of product C requires 1 hour of technical preparation, 5 hours of labor, and 1 kilogram of material. The available technical preparation time is 100 hours, labor time is 700 hours, and material is 400 kilograms. The company offers larger discounts for bulk purchases, as shown in Table 1-22. Determine the company's production plan to maximize profit.

\hline $0 \sim 40$ & 10 & $0 \sim 50$ & 6 & $0 \sim 100$ & 5 \\
\hline $40 \sim 100$ & 9 & $50 \sim 100$ & 4 & Above 100 & 4 \\
\hline $100 \sim 150$ & 8 & Above 100 & 3 & & \\
\hline Above 150 & 7 & \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{} & & \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# DATA: every numeric constant from the problem statement
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
DATA = {
    # Products and resources
    "products": ["A", "B", "C"],
    "resources": ["tech", "labor", "material"],

    # Resource usage per unit (rows = resource, cols = product)
    # "Each unit of A requires 1 hour prep, 10 hours labor, 3 kg material"
    "usage": {
        "tech":    {"A": 1, "B": 2, "C": 1},
        "labor":   {"A": 10, "B": 4, "C": 5},
        "material": {"A": 3, "B": 2, "C": 1},
    },

    # Available resources: tech 100 h, labor 700 h, material 400 kg
    "availability": {"tech": 100, "labor": 700, "material": 400},

    # Discount bands (Table 1-22). Each band: (lower, upper, profit_per_unit)
    # upper = None means unbounded above.
    "bands": {
        # Product A: 0-40 @10, 40-100 @9, 100-150 @8, above 150 @7
        "A": [(0, 40, 10), (40, 100, 9), (100, 150, 8), (150, None, 7)],
        # Product B: 0-50 @6, 50-100 @4, above 100 @3
        "B": [(0, 50, 6), (50, 100, 4), (100, None, 3)],
        # Product C: 0-100 @5, above 100 @4
        "C": [(0, 100, 5), (100, None, 4)],
    },

    # Big-M used to bound band variables (largest sensible production)
    "bigM": 1000,
}

GOLD_ANSWER = None


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    products = d["products"]
    resources = d["resources"]
    bands = d["bands"]
    bigM = d["bigM"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=products)
    model.R = pyo.Set(initialize=resources)

    # Band index set per product: (product, band_number)
    band_pairs = []
    for p in products:
        for k in range(len(bands[p])):
            band_pairs.append((p, k))
    model.B = pyo.Set(initialize=band_pairs, dimen=2)

    # Total production quantity per product (integer units)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Units allocated to each discount band (continuous; capacity capped by band)
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.B, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, bigM))

    # Binary: band is used / opened
    model.z = pyo.Var(model.B, domain=pyo.Binary)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Objective: maximize total profit
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(bands[p][k][2] * m.y[p, k] for (p, k) in m.B)
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Constraints
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    # Resource capacity constraints
    def resource_rule(m, r):
        return sum(d["usage"][r][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["availability"][r]
    model.resource_limit = pyo.Constraint(model.R, rule=resource_rule)

    # Total units = sum of band allocations
    def total_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] == sum(m.y[p, k] for k in range(len(bands[p])))
    model.total_units = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=total_rule)

    # Band capacity: y[p,k] <= width[p,k] * z[p,k]
    def band_cap_rule(m, p, k):
        lo, hi, _ = bands[p][k]
        width = bigM if hi is None else (hi - lo)
        return m.y[p, k] <= width * m.z[p, k]
    model.band_capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.B, rule=band_cap_rule)

    # Ordering: band k+1 can only be opened if band k is opened
    # (fill higher-profit bands first so discount structure is respected)
    def order_rule(m, p, k):
        if k == 0:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.z[p, k] <= m.z[p, k - 1]

    ordered_pairs = [(p, k) for (p, k) in band_pairs if k >= 1]
    model.band_order = pyo.Constraint(ordered_pairs, rule=order_rule)

    return model

    "tiers": {

        "B": [(0, 50, 6), (50, 100, 4), (100, None, 3)],
        "C": [(0, 100, 5), (100, None, 4)],
    },
    # big-M for the open-ended last tier (effectively unbounded upper)
    "open_upper": 100000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    products = d["products"]
    tiers = d["tiers"]

    # (product, tier_index) pairs
    seg_keys = [(p, s) for p in products for s in range(len(tiers[p]))]

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.P = pyo.Set(initialize=products)
    m.SEG = pyo.Set(initialize=seg_keys, dimen=2)

    # total production per product
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # quantity allocated to each tier
    m.seg = pyo.Var(m.SEG, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # tier activation binaries
    m.y = pyo.Var(m.SEG, within=pyo.Binary)

    # ---- Objective: maximize total profit ----
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(
            d["tiers"][p][s][2] * m.seg[p, s]
            for (p, s) in seg_keys
        )
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # ---- Resource capacity constraints ----
    def tech_rule(m):
        return sum(d["usage"][p]["tech"] * m.x[p] for p in products) <= d["avail"]["tech"]
    m.tech = pyo.Constraint(rule=tech_rule)

    def labor_rule(m):
        return sum(d["usage"][p]["labor"] * m.x[p] for p in products) <= d["avail"]["labor"]
    m.labor = pyo.Constraint(rule=labor_rule)

    def material_rule(m):
        return sum(d["usage"][p]["material"] * m.x[p] for p in products) <= d["avail"]["material"]
    m.material = pyo.Constraint(rule=material_rule)

    # ---- Linking: total production equals sum of tier allocations ----
    def link_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] == sum(m.seg[p, s] for s in range(len(tiers[p])))
    m.link = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=link_rule)

    # ---- Tier capacity (big-M via tier width) ----
    def tier_cap_rule(m, p, s):
        lower, upper, _ = tiers[p][s]
        width = (upper if upper is not None else d["open_upper"]) - lower
        return m.seg[p, s] <= width * m.y[p, s]
    m.tier_cap = pyo.Constraint(m.SEG, rule=tier_cap_rule)

    # ---- Tier ordering: must fill lower tiers before higher ones ----
    def tier_order_rule(m, p, s):
        if s == 0:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.y[p, s] <= m.y[p, s - 1]
    m.tier_order = pyo.Constraint(m.SEG, rule=tier_order_rule)

    # ---- First tier always active ----
    def first_tier_rule(m, p):
        return m.y[p, 0] == 1
    m.first_tier = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=first_tier_rule)

    return m

    }

    # cumulative width (units) of each bracket = upper - lower
    def width(p, k):
        up = d["brackets"][p][k][0]
        low = d["brackets"][p][k - 1][0] if k > 0 else 0
        return up - low

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # Sets
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------

    # flat set of (product, bracket) pairs

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # Variables
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # total units of each product  (units are indivisible -> integers)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # units of each product sold within each price bracket
    def y_bounds(m, p, k):
        up = d["brackets"][p][k][0]
        if up is None:                      # unbounded (last) bracket
            return (0, d["big_M"])
        return (0, width(p, k))

    model.y = pyo.Var(model.K, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=y_bounds)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # Objective: maximize total profit
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(
            d["brackets"][p][k][1] * m.y[p, k]
            for (p, k) in m.K
        )

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # Constraints
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # total produced of each product equals sum over its brackets
    def total_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] == sum(m.y[p, k] for k in bracket_index[p])
    model.total = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=total_rule)

    # technical preparation time availability  (<= 100)
    def tech_rule(m):
        return sum(d["tech"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["tech_avail"]

        return sum(d["material"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["material_avail"]
    model.material = pyo.Constraint(rule=material_rule)

_TIER_KEYS = []
_TIER_WIDTH = {}     # effective width used in the big-M band constraint
_TIER_RATE = {}      # profit per unit in that tier
_TIER_CUM = {}       # units needed below this tier before it can be used
_TIERS_OF = {}       # ordered tier indices for each product
_RATE_MIN = {}       # smallest profit rate (last tier) per product
_RATE_MAX = {}       # largest profit rate (first tier) per product

for _p, _tl in DATA["tiers"].items():
    _TIERS_OF[_p] = list(range(len(_tl)))
    _cum = 0
    for _k, (_w, _r) in enumerate(_tl):
        _TIER_KEYS.append((_p, _k))
        _TIER_WIDTH[(_p, _k)] = _w if _w is not None else DATA["bigM"]
        _TIER_RATE[(_p, _k)] = _r
        _TIER_CUM[(_p, _k)] = _cum          # capacity of all strictly-lower tiers

            _cum += _w
    _RATE_MAX[_p] = _tl[0][1]
    _RATE_MIN[_p] = _tl[-1][1]

DATA["tier_width"] = _TIER_WIDTH
DATA["tier_rate"] = _TIER_RATE
DATA["tier_cum"] = _TIER_CUM
DATA["tiers_of"] = _TIERS_OF
DATA["rate_max"] = _RATE_MAX
DATA["rate_min"] = _RATE_MIN


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"], ordered=True)
    m.R = pyo.Set(initialize=list(d["usage"].keys()), ordered=True)
    m.PT = pyo.Set(initialize=[tuple(k) for k in d["tier_keys"]], dimen=2, ordered=True)

    # ---- decision variables -------------------------------------------
    # total integer units produced of each product
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.P,
                  within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                  bounds=(0, d["bigM"]))

    # units of product p assigned to discount tier k
    m.y = pyo.Var(m.PT,
                  within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
                  bounds=(0, None))

    # indicator: lower tier (p, k-1) fully filled -> 1, used for sequential fill
    m.filled = pyo.Var(m.PT, within=pyo.Binary)

    # ---- objective: maximise total (tier-weighted) profit ------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["tier_rate"][p, k] * m.y[p, k] for p, k in m.PT)
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # ---- resource capacity constraints (one per resource) ------------
    def res_rule(m, r):
        return sum(d["usage"][r][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["avail"][r]
    m.resource_cap = pyo.Constraint(m.R, rule=res_rule)

    # ---- total produced equals sum over tiers ------------------------
    def link_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] == sum(m.y[p, k] for k in d["tiers_of"][p])
    m.link = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=link_rule)

    # ---- tier width caps ---------------------------------------------
    def width_rule(m, p, k):
        return m.y[p, k] <= d["tier_width"][p, k]
    m.width_cap = pyo.Constraint(m.PT, rule=width_rule)

    # ---- monotone fill: a tier above can receive units only if the
    # cumulative below is effectively full (indicator + big-M). ----------
    # For tier k>=1:  y[p,k] <= W_k * filled[p,k]
    #                 cum_below(k) - (1 - filled[p,k]) * M <= x_used_below
    def fill_bigM_rule(m, p, k):
        if k == 0:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.y[p, k] <= d["tier_width"][p, k] * m.filled[p, k]
    m.fill_bigM = pyo.Constraint(m.PT, rule=fill_bigM_rule)

    def fill_trigger_rule(m, p, k):
        if k == 0:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        cum = d["tier_cum"][p, k]
        # units placed strictly below tier k:
        below = sum(m.y[p, j] for j in range(k))
        M = d["bigM"]
        return cum - (1 - m.filled[p, k]) * M <= below
    m.fill_trigger = pyo.Constraint(m.PT, rule=fill_trigger_rule)

    # tier k=0 always "allowed": filled[p,0] fixed to 1
    def fill_base_rule(m, p):
        return m.filled[p, 0] == 1
    m.fill_base = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=fill_base_rule)

    return m

    },
    # big-M large enough for any tier count (upper bound of production)
    "bigM": 1000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    P = d["products"]
    R = d["resources"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=P)
    model.R = pyo.Set(initialize=R)

    # tier index set (0-based) per product
    tier_index = {p: list(range(len(d["tiers"][p]))) for p in P}
    model.K = pyo.Set(
        initialize=[(p, k) for p in P for k in tier_index[p]],
        dimen=2,
    )

    # ---- Variables ----
    # total units produced of each product
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # units sold within tier (p,k)
    model.t = pyo.Var(model.K, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # binray: tier (p,k) is "open"/used
    model.z = pyo.Var(model.K, domain=pyo.Binary)

    def tier_width(p, k):
        w = d["tiers"][p][k][0]
        return w if w is not None else d["bigM"]

    def tier_profit(p, k):
        return d["tiers"][p][k][1]

    # ---- Objective: maximize total profit ----
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(tier_profit(p, k) * model.t[p, k] for (p, k) in model.K),
        sense=pyo.maximize,
    )

    # ---- Constraints ----

    # 1) Tier capacity: units in tier (p,k) cannot exceed its width
    def cap_rule(m, p, k):
        return m.t[p, k] <= tier_width(p, k)
    model.tier_cap = pyo.Constraint(model.K, rule=cap_rule)

    # 2) Total produced of product p = sum of its tier units
    def balance_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] == sum(m.t[p, k] for k in tier_index[p])
    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=balance_rule)

    # 3) Ordering: tier (p,k) can be used only if previous tier is filled.
    #    t[p,k] <= width_k * z[p,k];  z[p,k] <= z[p,k-1]
    def open_rule(m, p, k):
        return m.t[p, k] <= tier_width(p, k) * m.z[p, k]
    model.open_link = pyo.Constraint(model.K, rule=open_rule)

    def order_rule(m, p, k):
        if k == 0:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.z[p, k] <= m.z[p, k - 1]
    model.order = pyo.Constraint(model.K, rule=order_rule)

    # 4) Resource constraints
    def res_rule(m, r):
        return sum(d["usage"][r][p] * m.x[p] for p in P) <= d["avail"][r]
    model.resource = pyo.Constraint(model.R, rule=res_rule)

    return model

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Problem data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Products: A, B, C
# Resources: technical preparation (hours), direct labour (hours), material (kg)
#
# Per-unit resource usage:
#   A: 1 tech, 10 labour, 3 material
#   B: 2 tech,  4 labour, 2 material
#   C: 1 tech,  5 labour, 1 material
#
# Availability: 100 tech, 700 labour, 400 material
#
# Profit is a piecewise (declining) function of sales volume for each product.
# We model each product's sales volume as the sum of quantities sold in each
# price tier, with tier quantities bounded by the tier width.  Because the
# profit per unit declines as volume increases, an optimal solution will
# always fill cheaper (higher-profit) tiers before moving to lower-profit
# tiers, so no explicit ordering constraint is required.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    "products": ["A", "B", "C"],
    "resources": ["tech", "labour", "material"],
    # resource usage a[resource][product]
    "usage": {
        "tech":     {"A": 1, "B": 2, "C": 1},
        "labour":   {"A": 10, "B": 4, "C": 5},
        "material": {"A": 3, "B": 2, "C": 1},
    },
    # resource availability
    "availability": {"tech": 100, "labour": 700, "material": 400},
    # profit tiers: for each product a list of (upper_bound, profit_per_unit)
    # upper_bound is the cumulative sales volume at the top of the tier.
    "tiers": {
        "A": [(40, 10), (100, 9), (150, 8), (None, 7)],
        "B": [(50, 6), (100, 4), (None, 3)],
        "C": [(100, 5), (None, 4)],
    },
    # big-M for the final (unbounded) tier: a safe upper bound on any product's
    # sales volume given the resources.  Labour is the tightest resource for
    # product C (5 h/unit, 700 h) -> 140; for A (10 h/unit) -> 70; for B
    # (4 h/unit) -> 175.  Use a generous common bound.
    "big_m": 1000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    products = d["products"]
    resources = d["resources"]

    # Build the set of (product, tier_index) pairs and the tier widths.
    tier_keys = []
    tier_width = {}
    tier_profit = {}
    for p in products:
        prev = 0
        for k, (ub, profit) in enumerate(d["tiers"][p]):
            tier_keys.append((p, k))
            if ub is None:
                width = d["big_m"]
            else:
                width = ub - prev
            tier_width[(p, k)] = width
            tier_profit[(p, k)] = profit
            if ub is not None:
                prev = ub

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=products, ordered=True)
    model.R = pyo.Set(initialize=resources, ordered=True)
    model.T = pyo.Set(initialize=tier_keys, dimen=2)

    # Decision variable: quantity sold of product p within tier k.
    def _tier_bounds(m, p, k):
        return (0, tier_width[(p, k)])

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.T, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=_tier_bounds)

    # Total sales volume of each product.
    def _total_rule(m, p):
        return sum(m.x[p, k] for k in range(len(d["tiers"][p])))

    model.total = pyo.Expression(model.P, rule=_total_rule)

    # Objective: maximize total profit.
    def _obj_rule(m):
        return sum(tier_profit[(p, k)] * m.x[p, k] for (p, k) in m.T)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=_obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # Resource capacity constraints.
    def _res_rule(m, r):
        return sum(d["usage"][r][p] * m.total[p] for p in m.P) <= d["availability"][r]

    model.resource_limit = pyo.Constraint(model.R, rule=_res_rule)

    return model

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision variables
#   xA : units of product A produced/sold        (NonNegativeReals)
#   xB : units of product B produced/sold        (NonNegativeReals)
#   xC : units of product C produced/sold        (NonNegativeReals)
#
#   Piecewise-linear profit via incremental (discount) segments.
#   For each product we introduce nonnegative segment variables that measure
#   how many units fall into each sales-volume band.  Because the per-unit
#   profit is non-increasing across bands, the LP relaxation automatically
#   fills cheaper (earlier) bands first, so no extra binaries are needed.
#
#   A-bands:  sA1 in [0,40]  profit 10
#             sA2 in [0,60]  profit  9
#             sA3 in [0,50]  profit  8
#             sA4 in [0,inf) profit  7
#   B-bands:  sB1 in [0,50]  profit  6
#             sB2 in [0,50]  profit  4
#             sB3 in [0,inf) profit  3
#   C-bands:  sC1 in [0,100] profit  5
#             sC2 in [0,inf) profit  4
#
# Objective (maximize): total profit from all sold units.
#
# Constraints
#   (1) Technical preparation:  1*xA + 2*xB + 1*xC <= 100
#   (2) Direct labor:          10*xA + 4*xB + 5*xC <= 700
#   (3) Material:               3*xA + 2*xB + 1*xC <= 400
#   (4) Linking: xA = sA1+sA2+sA3+sA4 ; xB = sB1+sB2+sB3 ; xC = sC1+sC2
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    # resource usage per unit
    "tech_A": 1, "tech_B": 2, "tech_C": 1,
    "labor_A": 10, "labor_B": 4, "labor_C": 5,
    "mat_A": 3, "mat_B": 2, "mat_C": 1,
    # resource availability
    "tech_avail": 100,
    "labor_avail": 700,
    "mat_avail": 400,
    # profit per unit in each band
    "pA1": 10, "pA2": 9, "pA3": 8, "pA4": 7,
    "pB1": 6, "pB2": 4, "pB3": 3,
    "pC1": 5, "pC2": 4,
    # band widths (upper bounds on segment variables)
    "wA1": 40, "wA2": 60, "wA3": 50,
    "wB1": 50, "wB2": 50,
    "wC1": 100,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ---- segment (band) variables -------------------------------------
    model.sA1 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["wA1"]))
    model.sA2 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["wA2"]))
    model.sA3 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["wA3"]))
    model.sA4 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    model.sB1 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["wB1"]))
    model.sB2 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["wB2"]))
    model.sB3 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    model.sC1 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["wC1"]))
    model.sC2 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ---- total production variables -----------------------------------
    model.xA = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.xB = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.xC = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ---- linking constraints ------------------------------------------
    def link_A_rule(m):
        return m.xA == m.sA1 + m.sA2 + m.sA3 + m.sA4
    model.link_A = pyo.Constraint(rule=link_A_rule)

    def link_B_rule(m):
        return m.xB == m.sB1 + m.sB2 + m.sB3
    model.link_B = pyo.Constraint(rule=link_B_rule)

    def link_C_rule(m):
        return m.xC == m.sC1 + m.sC2
    model.link_C = pyo.Constraint(rule=link_C_rule)

    # ---- resource constraints -----------------------------------------
    def tech_rule(m):
        return (d["tech_A"] * m.xA + d["tech_B"] * m.xB
                + d["tech_C"] * m.xC) <= d["tech_avail"]
    model.tech = pyo.Constraint(rule=tech_rule)

    def labor_rule(m):
        return (d["labor_A"] * m.xA + d["labor_B"] * m.xB
                + d["labor_C"] * m.xC) <= d["labor_avail"]
    model.labor = pyo.Constraint(rule=labor_rule)

    def mat_rule(m):
        return (d["mat_A"] * m.xA + d["mat_B"] * m.xB
                + d["mat_C"] * m.xC) <= d["mat_avail"]
    model.mat = pyo.Constraint(rule=mat_rule)

    # ---- objective -----------------------------------------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        return (d["pA1"] * m.sA1 + d["pA2"] * m.sA2
                + d["pA3"] * m.sA3 + d["pA4"] * m.sA4
                + d["pB1"] * m.sB1 + d["pB2"] * m.sB2
                + d["pB3"] * m.sB3
                + d["pC1"] * m.sC1 + d["pC2"] * m.sC2)
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model

    "bigM": 100000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    products = list(d["segments"].keys())

    # Segment index set: (product, segment_number)
    seg_index = [(p, s) for p in products for s in range(len(d["segments"][p]))]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=products)
    model.SEG = pyo.Set(initialize=seg_index, dimen=2)

    # x[p,s]: units sold in segment s of product p (integer)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.SEG, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # y[p,s]: binary, 1 if segment s is "active/reached" (used for fill ordering)
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.SEG, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Segment upper bounds
    def x_upper_rule(m, p, s):
        hi = d["segments"][p][s][1]
        if hi is None:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.x[p, s] <= hi
    model.x_upper = pyo.Constraint(model.SEG, rule=x_upper_rule)

    # Segment lower bounds (only enforced when segment is active)
    def x_lower_rule(m, p, s):
        lo = d["segments"][p][s][0]
        if lo == 0:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.x[p, s] >= lo * m.y[p, s]
    model.x_lower = pyo.Constraint(model.SEG, rule=x_lower_rule)

    # Fill-order linking: segment s can only be used if segment s-1 is filled.
    def order_rule(m, p, s):
        if s == 0:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        prev = s - 1
        prev_cap = d["segments"][p][prev][1]
        if prev_cap is None:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.x[p, prev] >= prev_cap * m.y[p, s]
    model.order = pyo.Constraint(model.SEG, rule=order_rule)

    def prep_rule(m):
        return sum(d["prep_usage"][p] * m.x[p, s]
                   for (p, s) in seg_index) <= d["prep_avail"]
    model.prep = pyo.Constraint(rule=prep_rule)

        return sum(d["labor_usage"][p] * m.x[p, s]
                   for (p, s) in seg_index) <= d["labor_avail"]
    model.labor = pyo.Constraint(rule=labor_rule)

        return sum(d["material_usage"][p] * m.x[p, s]
                   for (p, s) in seg_index) <= d["material_avail"]
    model.material = pyo.Constraint(rule=material_rule)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model
